title: Boot Targets and Startup Dependencies

content.intro: This lesson introduces boot targets and startup dependencies as part of boot process, init systems, and services. Begin with an observation you can safely repeat, then explain what the result tells you and what it does not prove.
content.why_it_matters: Explain startup flow and manage service units with distribution-aware tooling and recovery plans.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Startup and service management vary by init system. On systemd systems, units describe services, dependencies, timers, and other managed resources.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First, state what you expect from the example. Run it in the intended environment, capture standard output and any error message, and inspect the exit status where meaningful. Then connect the observation to this lesson: Boot Targets and Startup Dependencies. Do not infer more than the evidence supports.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake
content_blocks.text: A common mistake is to assume boot targets and startup dependencies behaves identically on every distribution, kernel, utility version, and administrative policy. Verify the installed tool and consult the matching manual before using the procedure elsewhere.

content_blocks.title: Safety and compatibility
content_blocks.text: This comparison does not install or remove packages; choose the tool for the actual distribution. For commands that edit files, manage services, change network/firewall state, partition disks, change permissions recursively, or alter boot settings, use an isolated VM, take a snapshot/backup, review the exact target, and prepare a recovery path before acting.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the command is missing, check whether the required package is installed and which distribution you are using. If access is denied, do not immediately escalate to root; confirm the target path, identity, and required permission. If the result differs, capture the command, output, version, and environment so the issue can be reproduced.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember the core relationship: Startup and service management vary by init system. On systemd systems, units describe services, dependencies, timers, and other managed resources. The goal is to explain the observed result, test a boundary case, and record a limitation rather than memorize a command in isolation.
